_readme: Product marketing framework (owner brief, 19 Nov 2026), schema v2. Platinum Smart-Heat® Gas: the two wall, ceiling and pole-mounted gas radiant heaters, named by output (23,600 and 39,800 BTU), never by the retired series numbers the site and manual still use. Matrix 1: what matters most to each buyer (w: 3 matters most, 2 matters, 1 nice to have) and the claim that resonates. Matrix 2: Tungsten Smart-Heat® Gas (left) against Platinum Gas (right), so sales know when to sell which; Tungsten Gas BTU stays unpublished (hard rule 3). Matrix 3: against Sunpak (Infrared Dynamics), Schwank supremeSchwank and the Lynx Eave Mounted Heater (factual, sourced, needs_approval Specification and compliance). Every Bromic fact is from product-facts (bromic.com read 29 Oct 2026) or Bromic's own cut sheet and manuals on pim.bromic.com (read 19 Nov 2026); competitor facts are from the makers' own spec sheets, manuals and pages. Competitor documents are dated (2012 to 2018 in places): every competitor row is to be re-checked before it is used outside sales training.
name: Platinum Smart-Heat® Gas

launch.summary: Platinum Gas is Bromic's design-led gas radiant heater: a ceramic-glass screen over a ceramic-tile burner, in black or stainless, for restaurant terraces, hotel and rooftop bars, pergolas and covered residential courtyards with a gas line. It sits above Tungsten Gas, which has the same heat areas, clearances and controls in a compact matte-black body at a lower list price.

m2_label.intro: Same heat areas, clearances, listing, controls and warranty; Platinum adds the ceramic-glass face and a stainless option, Tungsten is compact, matte black and lower priced.

m2.s1: ETL and cETL listing 4009079; electronic spark ignition with flame monitoring; for outdoor areas only.
m2.s2: ETL and cETL listing 4009079; electronic spark ignition with flame ionisation monitoring and lockout; for outdoor areas only.
m2.so_what: Sell on looks and budget; the safety story is identical.

m2.s1: Two models, heat areas 160 and 215 ft². Output: [[VERIFY: Tungsten Gas BTU; bromic.com and the 2026 manual give 26,000 and 43,000, the 2021 guide 39,800 — do not publish until confirmed — Product team]]
m2.s2: 23,600 and 39,800 BTU; heat areas 160 and 215 ft². The two manuals list the same burner part number.
m2.so_what: Same published coverage per size, so choose on the look and the budget, not on the heat area.

m2.s1: Matte black; front cover and flame protector over the burner (parts list); compact (19.3 in and 25.4 in long).
m2.s2: Signature ceramic-glass screen with reflector; Black or Stainless; 22.1 in and 29.8 in long.
m2.so_what: Where guests look up at the heater, Platinum's glass face and stainless option earn the premium.

m2.s1: Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off Controller, expansion board for BMS, manual wall switch; on/off only.
m2.s2: Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off Controller, expansion board for BMS, manual wall switch; on/off only.

m2.s1: IPX4; manual: designed to function in winds up to 10 mph (site: 8 mph); protect from rain.

sell_which.tungsten_gas: Sell Tungsten Gas where budget, count and a compact, all-black heater matter most: busy pubs, sports venues, back-of-house terraces, value-led residential, and sites with many heaters. List range $1,828–$2,087 on bromic.com.
sell_which.platinum_gas: Sell Platinum Gas where the heater is part of the design: front-of-house terraces, hotel and rooftop bars, fine dining, premium pergolas and residential courtyards, and wherever a stainless finish is asked for. List range $2,367–$2,657 on bromic.com.

m3.intro: The closest gas radiant alternatives a buyer will price against Platinum Gas in the US. Factual and sourced; competitor documents vary in date, so re-check before external use.

competitors.name: Sunpak S25 / S34 infrared patio heaters
competitors.owner: Infrared Dynamics, Yorba Linda, California (distributed by AEI Corporation)
competitors.why_closest: The most direct US match: a wall or ceiling-mounted ceramic infrared gas heater in two outputs (25,000 and 34,000 BTU), black or 304 stainless, sold to the same residential and restaurant buyers through dealers.

competitors.name: Schwank supremeSchwank (2300 series)
competitors.why_closest: The commercial-grade benchmark: ceramic-tile infrared gas heaters from 23,000 to 50,000 BTU with two-stage options, specified by mechanical engineers for hospitality and commercial patios.

competitors.name: Lynx Professional Eave Mounted Heater (LHEM48)
competitors.why_closest: The luxury residential benchmark sold beside premium outdoor kitchens: all-stainless, eave or wall mounted, 35,000 BTU infrared, with a wireless switch and remote.

rows.bromic: ETL and cETL listing 4009079; electronic spark ignition with flame ionisation sensing, 25 s safety time, lockout on failure; factory isolating valve (manual b3).

vs.sunpak: "CSA Design Certified"; "Direct Spark Ignition with Auto Re-light & Flame Sensor System" (c1).
vs.schwank: Guideline spec: tested to ANSI Z83.26 / CSA 2.37 (outdoor patio heaters) and ANSI Z83.19b / CSA 2.35b, certified by CSA; direct spark ignition and ionisation flame sensing (c6). Current page says "UL Certified" (c5).
vs.lynx: "complies with ANSI standard Z83.26-2007/ Z83.26a-2008 and CSA 2.37-2007", tested and approved by Intertek; spark ignition with heat-sensing safety pilot (c7).

COM.claim: Every option here is listed; choose on looks, controls and service.

INS.claim: Listed, flame-monitored and fitted with a factory isolating valve, like the best of the field.

ARC.claim: Equivalent listing and ignition safety; specify on design and placement.

BLD.claim: Inspection-ready, as you would expect of any listed heater.

RES.claim: The same flame-safety you would expect from any premium gas heater.

rows.bromic: 23,600 and 39,800 BTU, single stage; Bromic heat areas 160 and 215 ft² (b1, b2).

vs.sunpak: 25,000 and 34,000 BTU; TSR and TSH two-stage 25,000/34,000; "Approx. Coverage: 12' x 12' with minimal wind and at sea level" (c1).
vs.schwank: 23,000, 35,000 and 50,000 BTU; 2-stage option on the 48.25 in model (c5).
vs.lynx: "up to 35,000 BTU's", adjustable down to 27,000 (LP) and 24,000 (NG) (c7).

COM.claim: The larger Platinum puts out 39,800 BTU, more than a 34,000 BTU Sunpak or a 35,000 BTU Lynx; Schwank's two-stage reaches 50,000.

INS.claim: Compare input on the rating plates; each maker states coverage its own way, so size from the design plan.

ARC.claim: Specify by the design plan; output sits between Sunpak and Schwank's largest.

BLD.claim: Two sizes cover most pergolas and pavilions.

RES.claim: Up to 39,800 BTU from one heater, without a coverage race.

rows.bromic: Ceramic-glass screen with reflector; Black or Stainless (b2, b1).

vs.sunpak: Black powder coat or 304 stainless; SST models with curved front fascias; optional stainless, gloss black or antique bronze fascia trims (c1, c2).
vs.schwank: "finished in a sleek black" with black emissive coating (c5).
vs.lynx: All stainless, welded, "signature polished highlights" and a slim profile (c7).

COM.claim: A glass-fronted heater that suits the front of house, in black or stainless.

ARC.claim: A ceramic-glass face that reads as a design element, beside fascia-trimmed and polished-stainless alternatives.

BLD.claim: A premium look without custom trim.

RES.claim: A glass face in black or stainless, made to be seen.

rows.bromic: On/off only (no dimming, FAQ b1); Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off Controller in 1, 2 or 5 channels, up to 10 gas heaters a channel, expansion board for BMS, or manual wall switch (b1, b6). [[VERIFY: app, schedules and voice control for gas heaters through the On/Off Controller — Product team]]

vs.sunpak: S25/S34 on a standard wall switch; TSR two-stage with wireless remote and wall switch; TSH two-stage hardwired with a duplex switch (c1, c2).
vs.schwank: Single, double or triple switch, patio panel and remote; 2-stage option (c5); Patio Control Panel for zones (c6).
vs.lynx: Wireless on-off-hi-low wall switch and touch-screen remote; 6 heat levels on NG, 3 on LP (c7).

COM.claim: Run up to 10 heaters a channel from one Affinity controller, or tie the terrace into the BMS; for stepped heat, zone the heaters.

INS.claim: One Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off Controller switches up to 10 gas heaters a channel: fewer switches and runs than heater-by-heater wiring.

ARC.claim: Zone and BMS control through Affinity; competitors offer hi/low stages, Platinum offers zones.

BLD.claim: Zone switching from one controller across the site.

RES.claim: Simple on and off at the switch with Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls, by zone.

rows.bromic: Natural gas or propane, same rated input (b3).

vs.sunpak: Natural gas or propane, specify at order (c1).
vs.schwank: Natural gas or propane part numbers (c6).
vs.lynx: LHEM48NG and LHEM48LP; LP adjusts across fewer heat levels (c7).

COM.claim: Same choice of fuel as the field.

INS.claim: Factory NG or propane models, like every competitor here.

ARC.claim: Fuel is a site decision for every brand.

rows.bromic: Above: 3 ft without a deflector, 14 in with the heat deflector; sides 3 ft; 8 ft minimum to the floor (b3).

vs.sunpak: Horizontal: side 24 in, rear 17 in, ceiling 13 in, below 48 in; at 30°: ceiling 18 in (c1, c3).
vs.schwank: Guideline spec: above the heater no more than 5.5 in (23,000 BTU) or 7.5 in (35,000 BTU) horizontal, 9.5 in at 30° (c6).

rows.bromic: Wall bracket included; ceiling pole for two heaters back to back with gas and power inside the pole; tilt 0°, 10° or 20° (b3, b1).

vs.lynx: Eave, wall or fascia; tilt up to 30°; brackets give 10–18 in extension (c7).

battlecard.objection: Sunpak is made in California and costs less.
battlecard.answer: Compare what arrives in the box: Platinum ships with its wall bracket, flexible gas connector and a plug-in 110 V cord, where Sunpak S25 and S34 need an external 24 V transformer and mounting kit. Platinum's larger model is 39,800 BTU against Sunpak's 34,000.

battlecard.objection: Schwank needs far less clearance above.
battlecard.answer: That is true: Schwank publishes 5.5 to 9.5 in. With the dual-layer stainless heat deflector, Platinum needs 14 in above. Our free design plan places each heater and deflector for your ceiling.

battlecard.objection: Lynx gives me six heat levels from a remote.
battlecard.answer: Platinum is on/off by design and switches by zone: one Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off Controller runs up to 10 gas heaters a channel, so you turn areas on and off as the terrace fills.

battlecard.objection: Can it go in our enclosed patio room?
battlecard.answer: No. Platinum Gas is for outdoor areas only, as the manual defines them, for example under a roof with no more than two walls. For a space that does not meet that definition, talk to our design team.

battlecard.objection: Why pay more than for Tungsten Gas?
battlecard.answer: You get the same coverage, clearances, controls and warranty either way. Platinum adds the ceramic-glass face and a stainless option for spaces where guests see the heater; Tungsten is compact and matte black at a lower list price.

battlecard.objection: Will it work on our windy waterfront?
battlecard.answer: Platinum is designed to function in winds up to 10 mph and works best under cover, where heat loss is greatest. In salt air, plan more frequent checks; for marine craft and exposed coastal sites, look at Platinum Electric Marine.
